newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia overnight at 8.0 pct vs 6.5, still rising.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia overnight at 8.0 pct vs 6.5, still rising.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate for the long weekend rose to 8.0 percent against 6.5 previously due to heavy borrowing by commercial banks towards close of trading on Friday, dealers said.
Within a few minutes the overnight rate rose further to 8.7 percent as the banks, all of them large domestic ones, continued to look for funds to cover their positions, the dealers said.
They said the overnight was unlikely to rise further as 8.7 was perceived as the unspoken limit imposed by Bank Negara.
"Big local banks have come in now and are pushing up rates. They seem to be very short," a dealer with a local bank said.
Dealers said they did not know why the banks were short.
"It is possible that the heavy buying in KLIBOR futures may have brought in some central bank intervention," another dealer said.
Earlier, other interbank rates were a shade easier as the market adjusted to the higher liquidity that came into the system two days ago.
They said interbank rates could have fallen slightly more but that was prevented by the presence of finance companies and a few merchant banks, which are considered higher risk borrowers.
"A few poor names are in the market. But the market is very quiet," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
One-week money was at 6.90/7.00 percent against 7.10/15, two-week was at 7.00/15 against 7.15/20 and one-month at 7.18/21 against 7.20/23.
Three-month rate was at 7.20/25 percent against 7.23/25 and six-month at 7.27/30 against 7.28/35.

Dealers said the interbank rates have been easy since Thursday, after fresh liquidity, widely believed to be overseas funds returning to invest in the stock market, entered the system late on Wednesday.
Dealers said the fall was expected to be limited to around the current levels as Bank Negara has made clear it will maintain its tight monetary policy for the rest of the year.
